title: Hire Right App — Log Observability Genie
description: Ask plain-English questions about the Hire Right Databricks App's runtime logs: did a deployment fail and why, which features people use, which requests errored or were slow, whether the app can reach the agent endpoint, and who signed in. Powered by Databricks Apps OpenTelemetry logs in Unity Catalog.
sample_questions: Did any app deployments fail, and why?
Which app features are used the most, and are any returning errors?
Show me every warning and error since the last deployment.
Can the app reach the Hire Right agent endpoint, or are calls failing?
Who is using the app and when is it busiest?
Which candidates were viewed the most in the app?

description: VARIANT key/value map. Key app.log_source = BUILD (deploy process), HTTP (proxy access log), APP (app stdout). Key app.deployment_id = deployment. System events set event.name (e.g. app.auth) instead. Read with attributes:['key']::string.
VARIANT holding the raw log line text. Format depends on app.log_source. Read with body::string.

content:
## PURPOSE
- Explain the Hire Right Databricks App's runtime logs to app owners: deploy health, errors, dependency failures, and usage — in plain English.
- Source: OpenTelemetry logs that Databricks Apps exports to __CATALOG__.__SCHEMA__.__PREFIX___otel_logs, flattened into the v_app_* views.

## HOW THE RAW LOG TABLE WORKS
- __PREFIX___otel_logs has one row per log line. Most OTel columns (trace_id, span_id, event_name, severity_number, flags, schema URLs) are always empty. The meaning lives in time, attributes (a VARIANT key/value map) and body (the log text).
- The key field is attributes['app.log_source']. It says which process wrote the line:
- BUILD = the deployment/build process. Example body: "Starting app with command: [python app.py]", "Deployment … ended in 2.53s", "[ERROR] app exited unexpectedly". What we pull out: deployment ID, start command, deploy duration, success/failure, error message -> v_app_deployments.
- HTTP = the Databricks Apps proxy access log, one line per user request. Body format: client IP, user_id@workspace_id, [timestamp], "METHOD path", status, bytes, referer, user agent. What we pull out: endpoint, app feature, status, bytes, user, browser, approximate duration -> v_app_http_requests.
- APP = the app's own stdout/stderr (uvicorn + Python logging). Example body: "POST /api/chat/stream 200 OK", "INFO:httpx:HTTP Request: POST …/serving-endpoints/hire-right-agent-endpoint/invocations 403 Forbidden", "WARNING:db:… permission denied". What we pull out: warnings, errors, tracebacks, outbound calls to dependencies -> v_app_log_events, v_app_outbound_calls.
- attributes['app.deployment_id'] = the deployment that wrote the line (BUILD, APP, HTTP).
- Platform system events have no app.log_source; instead attributes['event.name'] is set (e.g. app.auth with app.auth.outcome, app.auth.reason, enduser.id) and service_name is NULL -> v_app_auth_events.

## DISAMBIGUATION
- "requests", "usage", "traffic", "features" -> v_app_http_requests. In v_app_log_events never count message_category = 'Request echo' (uvicorn's duplicate of a proxy request line).
- "errors" with no qualifier -> severity ERROR/WARN in v_app_log_events plus is_error in v_app_outbound_calls and v_app_http_requests.
- "why did the deploy fail" / "why is the app down" -> v_app_deployments.failure_reason and start_command.
- "slow" / "latency" -> v_app_http_requests.approx_duration_seconds; precise latency is not in the logs.

## DATA QUALITY NOTES
- /api/chat/stream can return 200 to the user even when the agent endpoint call failed (streaming starts first). Check v_app_outbound_calls for 403/5xx.
- Raw severity_text is UNKNOWN for HTTP lines; use the normalized severity column.
- user_id is a numeric Databricks user ID; emails appear only in v_app_auth_events.
- All times are UTC.

## CONSTRAINTS
- Prefer the v_app_* views. Query __PREFIX___otel_logs directly only when no view covers the question.

## Instructions you must follow when providing summaries
- State the time range and the number of log lines or requests behind the answer.
- When reporting an error, explain in one plain-English sentence what it means for the app.

question: Did any deployments fail, and why?
sql:
SELECT v_app_deployments.started_at,
       v_app_deployments.deployment_id,
       v_app_deployments.outcome,
       v_app_deployments.start_command,
       v_app_deployments.failure_reason,
       v_app_deployments.deploy_seconds
FROM __CATALOG__.__SCHEMA__.v_app_deployments
ORDER BY v_app_deployments.started_at DESC

question: Which app features are used most, and what is their error rate?
sql:
SELECT v_app_http_requests.app_feature,
       COUNT(*) AS requests,
       COUNT(DISTINCT v_app_http_requests.user_id) AS users,
       COUNT_IF(v_app_http_requests.is_error) AS errors,
       ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN v_app_http_requests.is_error THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) * 100, 1) AS error_rate_pct
FROM __CATALOG__.__SCHEMA__.v_app_http_requests
GROUP BY v_app_http_requests.app_feature
ORDER BY requests DESC

question: Show warnings and errors logged since the most recent deployment started.
sql:
SELECT v_app_log_events.event_time,
       v_app_log_events.log_source,
       v_app_log_events.severity,
       v_app_log_events.message_category,
       v_app_log_events.logger_name,
       v_app_log_events.message
FROM __CATALOG__.__SCHEMA__.v_app_log_events
WHERE v_app_log_events.severity IN ('ERROR', 'WARN')
  AND v_app_log_events.event_time >= (SELECT MAX(v_app_deployments.started_at) FROM __CATALOG__.__SCHEMA__.v_app_deployments)
ORDER BY v_app_log_events.event_time DESC

question: Are the app's calls to its dependencies succeeding?
sql:
SELECT v_app_outbound_calls.target_service,
       v_app_outbound_calls.status_code,
       v_app_outbound_calls.status_reason,
       COUNT(*) AS calls,
       MIN(v_app_outbound_calls.call_time) AS first_seen,
       MAX(v_app_outbound_calls.call_time) AS last_seen
FROM __CATALOG__.__SCHEMA__.v_app_outbound_calls
GROUP BY v_app_outbound_calls.target_service, v_app_outbound_calls.status_code, v_app_outbound_calls.status_reason
ORDER BY calls DESC

question: When is the app busiest, by hour?
sql:
SELECT v_app_http_requests.request_hour,
       COUNT(*) AS requests,
       COUNT(DISTINCT v_app_http_requests.user_id) AS users
FROM __CATALOG__.__SCHEMA__.v_app_http_requests
GROUP BY v_app_http_requests.request_hour
ORDER BY v_app_http_requests.request_hour

question: Which requests took the longest?
sql:
SELECT v_app_http_requests.request_time,
       v_app_http_requests.app_feature,
       v_app_http_requests.http_method,
       v_app_http_requests.path,
       v_app_http_requests.status_code,
       v_app_http_requests.approx_duration_seconds
FROM __CATALOG__.__SCHEMA__.v_app_http_requests
ORDER BY v_app_http_requests.approx_duration_seconds DESC
LIMIT 10

question: Which log sources and attribute keys appear in the raw log table?
sql:
SELECT COALESCE(__PREFIX___otel_logs.attributes:['app.log_source']::string, 'SYSTEM: ' || __PREFIX___otel_logs.attributes:['event.name']::string) AS log_source,
       attr_key,
       COUNT(*) AS log_lines
FROM __CATALOG__.__SCHEMA__.__PREFIX___otel_logs
LATERAL VIEW explode(map_keys(from_json(__PREFIX___otel_logs.attributes::string, 'map<string,string>'))) k AS attr_key
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY log_source, log_lines DESC
AVG(CASE WHEN v_app_http_requests.is_error THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) * 100

question: How many app deployments have failed?

content:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS failed_deployments
FROM __CATALOG__.__SCHEMA__.v_app_deployments
WHERE v_app_deployments.outcome = 'Failed'

question: Which start command did the most recent failed deployment use?

content:
SELECT v_app_deployments.start_command
FROM __CATALOG__.__SCHEMA__.v_app_deployments
WHERE v_app_deployments.outcome = 'Failed'
ORDER BY v_app_deployments.started_at DESC
LIMIT 1

question: How many user HTTP requests has the app served in total?
How many outbound calls to the agent serving endpoint returned 403?

content:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS forbidden_calls
FROM __CATALOG__.__SCHEMA__.v_app_outbound_calls
WHERE v_app_outbound_calls.target_service = 'Serving endpoint: hire-right-agent-endpoint'
  AND v_app_outbound_calls.status_code = 403

question: How many distinct users have made requests to the app?
How many warning-level log lines has the app written?

content:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS warnings
FROM __CATALOG__.__SCHEMA__.v_app_log_events
WHERE v_app_log_events.severity = 'WARN'
